On iteration 1 recall 0.9365 sat 0.0330 below specificity 0.9695 and on iteration 2 recall 0.9171 sat 0.0471 below specificity 0.9642 — the same sign both times, so the default rule is cutting on the conservative side of the ranking and the positive class is under-weighted. balanced_accuracy is the mean of recall and specificity, so pulling the cut toward the positive class trades a little specificity for more recall and should move the mean up, with cut_headroom 0.0048 on iteration 1 bounding how much any cut of this ranking can yield. If the sign flips (recall > specificity) the crossing will be bracketed and the last two attempts can settle on an explicit intermediate weight map; if it does not flip, the ranking axis is the only remaining owner and a bagging-family swap becomes the next move.
